candidates.rationale: Sustained low traded value over 3 days is priced as an illiquidity risk premium: investors demand compensation for the higher trading cost of hard-to-trade names, so inverted rank of smoothed dollar volume should lead higher forward returns for the least liquid names.
Same illiquidity-premium mechanism as a 3-day window but measured over 8 days: persistently thin traded value marks names that require a return premium to compensate holders for higher trading costs.

A standardized 6-day average share-volume level proxies short-lived investor attention; freshly crowded, high-volume names keep absorbing momentum flow that pushes prices further, so the level itself carries near-term return information.

The worst (minimum) traded value seen over the last 15 days measures tail liquidity risk better than an average; a low liquidity floor means a holder could be trapped in a one-sided market, so inverted rank of that floor proxies a compensated liquidity risk premium.

Same tail-liquidity-risk mechanism as the 15-day version, measured over 25 days: a persistently low liquidity floor over a longer window is a stronger signature of structural (not one-off) illiquidity risk.

The coefficient of variation of traded value over 21 days measures how unpredictable a name's liquidity supply is; investors require compensation for that liquidity uncertainty, so its rank should positively predict returns.
Same liquidity-uncertainty mechanism as the 21-day version measured over 35 days, capturing a slightly more persistent regime of unstable trading interest that commands a risk premium.

A 63-day average traded-value level identifies structurally illiquid names; the liquidity discount they trade at is a slow-moving, capital-structure-like characteristic, so inverted rank of the long-run level predicts a persistent return premium.
Same structural-illiquidity-premium mechanism measured over a half-year (126-day) window, which better isolates persistent liquidity classification from temporary liquidity dips.
Same structural-illiquidity-premium mechanism measured over a full year, capturing the most durable component of a stock's liquidity classification within the large-cap universe.

Share volume scaled by price and smoothed over 90 days measures durable retail/lottery-style participation concentrated in lower-priced names; that persistent noise-trader demand keeps such names overpriced relative to fundamentals.
Same lottery-demand mechanism as the 90-day version measured over 180 days, isolating the most durable low-priced-stock speculative-volume signature.

Same-day cross-sectional traded-value rank captures a transient liquidity/attention shock; capital chasing an already-crowded name creates short-lived price pressure that reverses, giving contrarian next-day predictability.

A same-day standardized burst in share volume relative to the whole universe flags acute attention that produces a temporary price dislocation subsequently reversed as the crowd's liquidity demand fades.
Same-day dollar volume scaled by price approximates instantaneous share turnover; abrupt turnover spikes are dominated by short-horizon, non-informational liquidity demand that reverts quickly.
The gap between a stock's share-count-volume rank and its dollar-value rank isolates low-priced-stock volume concentration, a retail/lottery-demand signature that predicts subsequent reversal.

Ranking today's traded value against only its own trailing 5 days isolates idiosyncratic liquidity surges from market-wide ones; an idiosyncratic surge is dominated by short-lived liquidity trading that mean-reverts.

A stock's own 21-day volume percentile captures whether today's participation is elevated relative to its recent regime; elevated self-relative volume signals unresolved information flow still being absorbed, predicting continuation over the window's horizon.
Same self-relative-participation mechanism as the 21-day version but measured against a 40-day regime, capturing a slightly slower-resolving information-absorption process.

A small offset from the peak means the highest traded value in the last 63 days occurred very recently; a fresh, unresolved liquidity/information shock of that scale keeps being absorbed by the market, predicting continued drift over the remainder of the regime.
Same fresh-liquidity-shock mechanism as the 63-day version but measured against a half-year regime, capturing larger, less frequent capital-flow events.
Same fresh-liquidity-shock mechanism measured against a 200-day regime, isolating the single largest capital-flow event of the past year and how recently it occurred.

Days since the 90-day volume trough marks a stock re-emerging from a dry spell in participation; renewed trading interest after a liquidity lull triggers fresh price discovery that a static liquidity level would miss.
Same re-emergence-from-a-dry-spell mechanism as the 90-day version but measured against a 150-day regime, capturing longer liquidity droughts before renewed participation begins.

A 2-day average volume running above its own 5-day baseline signals a fresh, still-unfolding information event; because new information diffuses gradually through a large-cap name, the resulting order-flow imbalance predicts short-horizon continuation.
Same short-baseline volume-acceleration mechanism as the 2/5-day pair, measured over a slightly wider 3/8-day pair to reduce single-day noise while remaining a fast-decaying signal.

An exponentially weighted 4-day volume level relative to its 10-day counterpart reacts to fresh participation shifts while damping single-day noise, capturing an accelerating liquidity regime that precedes continued price adjustment.

A rising ratio of 5-day to 15-day smoothed dollar volume shows capital committing to a name faster than its recent norm; sustained capital commitment of this kind precedes continued institutional accumulation and price drift.
Same capital-commitment-acceleration mechanism as the 5/15-day pair, measured over an 8/21-day pair to capture a slightly slower institutional accumulation regime.
Volume variability over 12 days rising relative to its 30-day norm signals building disagreement/information asymmetry among traders; such regime shifts in uncertainty precede resolving price moves.
Same building-disagreement mechanism as the 12/30-day pair, measured over a 14/35-day pair to confirm the volume-volatility regime shift persists over a slightly longer horizon.

The ratio of the single busiest day to the 63-day average volume measures how concentrated (spiky) participation has been; a single dominant liquidity event embeds information that diffuses slowly across a quarter-scale window, predicting continued drift.
Same spikiness-of-participation mechanism as the 63-day version measured over 126 days, isolating the dominant liquidity event of the past half-year relative to its typical baseline.

Capital flow measured over 21 days relative to its 63-day baseline identifies a structural pickup in institutional interest; such regime changes in sponsorship unwind slowly, supporting continued price drift over several months.
Same structural-sponsorship-pickup mechanism as the 21/63-day pair, measured over a 25/90-day pair to confirm the capital-flow regime shift over a longer baseline.
Same structural-sponsorship-pickup mechanism measured over a 30/100-day pair, capturing a slower-forming institutional accumulation regime.

A 40-day smoothed participation level elevated relative to its 150-day norm marks a durable shift in investor attention; durable attention shifts in large caps are associated with slow multi-month re-rating as coverage catches up.
Same durable-attention-shift mechanism as the 40/150-day pair, measured over a 21/126-day pair to capture a somewhat faster-forming coverage change.

Today's raw volume relative to its 3-day baseline is a same-day surprise measure; unexpected participation spikes reflect new information hitting the tape that the market has not yet fully processed, predicting a short-lived directional continuation.
Same same-day volume-surprise mechanism as the 3-day baseline, measured against a 5-day baseline to slightly reduce single-day baseline noise.
Same same-day volume-surprise mechanism measured against a 10-day baseline, capturing surprise relative to a full two-week trading regime.

Today's capital flow relative to its 4-day norm measures an immediate liquidity shock; abrupt capital commitment tends to precede continued order-flow pressure in the same direction over the next few sessions.
Same immediate-liquidity-shock mechanism as the 4-day baseline, measured against an 8-day baseline to smooth the reference level slightly.

The 15-day raw change in volume, standardized by its own 15-day volatility, is a volume-surprise z-score that jumps whenever fresh participation departs from its recent regime, flagging an information event still being priced in.
Same volume-surprise z-score mechanism as the 15-day version, measured over 21 days to align with a monthly participation regime.
Same volume-surprise z-score mechanism measured over 30 days, capturing a slower-building participation shift.

A small offset to the volume peak within the last 18 days indicates the biggest liquidity/attention shock of this window is still fresh; the market keeps absorbing a recent large order-flow imbalance, predicting continued drift.
Same fresh-order-flow-imbalance mechanism as the 18-day version, measured over 25 days to capture a slightly larger recent participation shock.

The direction of the 63-day change in volume, weighted by the stock's own 63-day volume percentile, flags names undergoing a decisive, self-relative participation regime shift rather than routine noise, which precedes continued price adjustment.
Same decisive-regime-shift mechanism as the 63-day version, measured over 100 days to capture a slower, more structural participation change.
Same decisive-regime-shift mechanism applied to capital flow rather than share count over 90 days, capturing a structural change in institutional dollar commitment.

A short-window change in smoothed volume, standardized against its 126-day volatility, flags a fresh acceleration in participation relative to a slow-moving liquidity regime, indicating information is still being incorporated.
Same fresh-acceleration-against-a-slow-regime mechanism as the previous pair, measured with an 8-day EMA, 30-day change, and 150-day volatility baseline for a slower overall horizon.
Same fresh-acceleration mechanism applied to capital flow over a 10-day EMA, 40-day change, and 180-day volatility baseline, capturing a structural institutional-flow inflection.

A positive 3-day correlation between volume and price means the recent trend has been confirmed by participation rather than drifting on thin liquidity; volume-confirmed trends are more likely information-driven and continue.
Same volume-confirms-trend mechanism as the 3-day version, measured over 6 days to reduce single-day noise in the correlation estimate.
Same volume-confirms-trend mechanism measured over 10 days, capturing a slightly more established participation-price relationship.

Volume co-moving with the size of daily returns over 5 days is the classic signature of new information hitting the tape; stocks currently showing this linkage are mid-way through an information event, predicting continued volatility-adjusted drift.
Same information-event signature as the 5-day version, measured over 8 days to confirm the volume-volatility linkage is not a single-day artifact.

Capital flow that lines up with the direction of returns over 15 days shows genuine buying/selling pressure rather than noise; such flow-confirmed moves are more persistent than unconfirmed price changes.
Same flow-confirmed-move mechanism as the 15-day version, measured over 21 days to align with a monthly return-flow regime.
Same flow-confirmed-move mechanism measured over 30 days, capturing a slightly more persistent buying/selling pressure regime.

A negative 18-day volume-return correlation means rallies are occurring on shrinking participation (or declines on rising participation) - a classic distribution/accumulation divergence that historically precedes a reversal once the unconfirmed move exhausts itself.
Same distribution/accumulation-divergence mechanism as the 18-day version, measured over 25 days to confirm the unconfirmed move is a persistent divergence rather than noise.

A 63-day volume-return covariance, standardized by the scale of capital flow, isolates the structural strength of order-flow-confirmed price moves independent of a stock's absolute liquidity level, a persistent characteristic across quarters.
Same standardized order-flow-confirmation mechanism as the 63-day version, measured over 90 days for a somewhat more durable estimate.
Same standardized order-flow-confirmation mechanism measured over a half-year, isolating the most persistent component of flow-confirmed price strength.

Whether daily range expands together with volume over 75 days reveals whether order flow moves price (informed trading, wide range needed to clear volume) or is absorbed without much price impact (deep, liquid market); the former signals durable information content that continues to be priced in.
Same range-volume linkage mechanism as the 75-day version, measured over 120 days to isolate a more structural informed-trading regime versus deep-market absorption.
Amihud-style price impact: how much a stock moves per dollar traded measures immediate illiquidity; investors demand higher expected returns to hold names with high per-dollar price impact.
Same Amihud price-impact mechanism as the 2-day version, measured against a 4-day baseline to slightly smooth the liquidity denominator.
Same Amihud price-impact mechanism measured against a 6-day baseline, capturing immediate illiquidity relative to a slightly longer reference.

Averaging daily price-impact-per-dollar-traded over 5 days gives a smoother illiquidity estimate than a single day's return, but still updates with each new noisy daily observation, and predicts the compensation liquidity-constrained investors require.
Same smoothed Amihud-illiquidity mechanism as the 5-day version, measured over 10 days for a somewhat more stable illiquidity estimate.

Weighting today's return direction by how far volume sits above its 12-day baseline isolates conviction-backed moves; price changes accompanied by abnormal participation are more likely driven by informed trading and continue rather than fade.
Same conviction-backed-move mechanism as the 12-day version, measured against a 21-day baseline for a monthly participation reference.

A positive volume-return relationship carries more informational weight when it occurs in an already liquid, closely watched name, since informed trading is easier to disguise there; this interaction isolates genuinely informative flow-confirmed moves.
Same liquidity-weighted flow-confirmation mechanism as the 15-day version, measured over 30 days to capture a more established relationship.

Capital flow that scales with the magnitude of returns over a 50-day window is the fingerprint of a sustained, information-driven trading regime rather than a one-off event, and such regimes take months to fully resolve into price.
Same sustained information-driven-regime mechanism as the 50-day version, measured over 100 days to isolate the most durable component of the linkage.

The absolute strength (regardless of sign) of the 63-day volume-return relationship measures how much of a stock's recent price action is participation-confirmed versus noise; strongly confirmed regimes, whichever direction, are more likely to persist than to mean-revert.
Same participation-confirmation-strength mechanism as the 63-day version, measured over a half-year for a more durable estimate of confirmed regimes.
Same participation-confirmation-strength mechanism measured over 200 days, isolating the most structural component of volume-return linkage.
Same participation-confirmation-strength mechanism applied to capital flow rather than share count over 90 days, capturing dollar-weighted conviction regardless of direction.

A 3-day average of the daily high-low range relative to price approximates the effective bid-ask spread investors pay to trade; investors require compensation for this trading-cost drag, so its level should positively predict forward returns.
Same effective-spread mechanism as the 3-day version, measured over 6 days to reduce single-day range noise in the trading-cost estimate.
Averaging how much price range is generated per share traded over 5 days is a Kyle's-lambda-style market-depth measure; thinner markets (high impact per share) demand a larger risk premium.
Same market-depth mechanism as the 5-day version, measured over 8 days for a slightly more stable per-share price-impact estimate.

Price range generated per dollar traded, averaged over 12 days, measures market depth on a capital basis rather than a share basis, capturing an illiquidity premium comparable across differently priced large caps.
Same capital-basis market-depth mechanism as the 12-day version, measured over 21 days for a monthly illiquidity-premium estimate.

The 18-day volatility of the relative daily range measures how unpredictable a name's trading cost is from day to day; that liquidity-cost uncertainty itself is a priced risk factor distinct from the average cost level.
Same liquidity-cost-uncertainty mechanism as the 18-day version, measured over 30 days to confirm the instability persists beyond a short window.

A 63-day average relative range is a slow-moving, structural proxy for a name's typical effective spread; structurally wide-spread names carry a persistent illiquidity discount that resolves only over long holding periods.
Same structural-effective-spread mechanism as the 63-day version, measured over a half-year for the most durable estimate of typical trading cost.

Averaging how much of the day's range survives from open to close over 90 days measures trend efficiency; names that persistently close near their extreme rather than round-tripping exhibit more efficient, information-driven price discovery that continues to compound.
Same trend-efficiency mechanism as the 90-day version, measured over 150 days to isolate the most durable component of directional price discovery.

Today's raw high-low range relative to price is a same-day effective-spread proxy; an unusually wide range signals acute, short-lived difficulty in transacting that a liquidity-sensitive investor is compensated for bearing overnight.

Today's range relative to its own 5-day norm flags a sudden liquidity/volatility shock; range expansions of this kind are associated with information events whose price impact keeps unwinding over the next few sessions.
Same range-expansion-shock mechanism as the 5-day version, measured against a 10-day norm to confirm the expansion is unusual relative to a longer baseline.

Same-day range generated per share traded is an instantaneous price-impact coefficient; a sudden spike in per-share impact reveals a temporary lack of depth that is compensated by higher near-term expected returns.

Unusually costly price discovery (wide range per dollar traded) happening in a name with contemporaneously high share volume is a distress signature - even active trading isn't enough to keep the market orderly - a state that commands a same-day liquidity-risk premium.

The fraction of today's range that survived from open to close measures same-day directional conviction; a high close-location value shows one-sided order flow overwhelming the other side, a short-lived imbalance that tends to carry into the next session.

Days since the widest single-day range in the last 63 days marks how long ago the most acute liquidity event of this regime occurred; the market keeps re-testing that event's price level until enough time has passed, so its recency itself carries return information.
Same acute-liquidity-event-recency mechanism as the 63-day version, measured over a half-year to capture the largest range event of a longer regime.

A stock whose range rank sits far above its liquidity rank is generating more price movement than its trading activity would predict, a same-day mismatch between volatility and depth that identifies acute, not-yet-resolved illiquidity stress.
Same volatility-versus-depth mismatch mechanism as the close-normalized version, using per-share range instead to isolate the same-day illiquidity-stress signature on a share-count basis.

A 90-day average relative range is a slow-moving, structural proxy for a name's typical effective spread; structurally wide-spread names carry a persistent illiquidity discount that resolves only over long holding periods.
The 40-day volatility of per-share price impact captures regime shifts in market depth; increasingly unstable depth is itself a priced liquidity-risk characteristic distinct from its average level.

Today's range relative to its own 21-day norm flags a liquidity/volatility shock at a slightly longer horizon than a pure overnight measure, associated with information events that continue unwinding over the following weeks.

Days since the tightest single-day range in the last 100 days marks how long a stock has gone without a genuine liquidity test; a long-quiet regime ending is when the next real price-discovery event is most informative.

Highly levered firms are least able to absorb a liquidity drought, so a 5-day inverted liquidity-level rank scaled by leverage isolates which structurally illiquid names carry the sharpest distress risk.

Durable profitability partly compensates for the extra risk of holding a structurally illiquid name, so scaling return-on-assets by an inverted liquidity rank isolates a cleaner quality-adjusted liquidity premium.

Low accounting quality is harder for arbitrageurs to correct when a name is also structurally illiquid, so the interaction shows the mispricing persisting longer and compounding with the liquidity discount.
High-quality but under-followed names take longer to be discovered, so profitability confirmed by structurally low liquidity marks a deeper, slower-resolving mispricing.
Cheap-on-book names that are also thinly traded stack a value premium on top of a liquidity premium, since both frictions independently require compensation.
Operationally efficient firms with persistently low trading activity are unlikely to be crowded, so the combination flags an under-owned quality name.

Firms sustaining strong operating margins while remaining structurally illiquid are less likely to have that margin strength already arbitraged into the price, since institutional attention has not yet arrived.
Capital-structure risk and structural illiquidity both intensify in a stress scenario, so their product proxies compounded tail risk that is priced with a premium over long horizons.
Durable margin strength in a structurally thin-liquidity name signals a business the market has not yet had reason to crowd into, a slow-resolving discovery opportunity.
Sustained profitability paired with a persistently low liquidity level marks quality hiding in an under-owned corner of the large-cap universe.
A durable earnings-per-share level in a structurally illiquid name is compensation stacked on top of an unrecognized-quality discount, since low coverage delays the market's re-rating.

Leverage amplifies the consequences of unpredictable liquidity supply, so scaling leverage by the coefficient of variation of traded value isolates firms most exposed to a liquidity-driven funding squeeze.
A same-day liquidity/attention shock is more dangerous for a highly levered balance sheet, so interacting leverage with a standardized same-day liquidity level flags acute margin-call-style risk.
A sudden burst of attention on a name with questionable earnings quality is when informed short-sellers are most likely acting on the accrual signal, so the interaction targets that specific moment.
A same-day attention spike hitting a genuinely profitable name is more likely to reflect real news than noise, so quality filters which liquidity shocks matter.
An efficient asset base combined with a same-day volume shock flags operationally sound firms suddenly drawing fresh scrutiny, the moment a stale efficiency story is most likely to be repriced.
Weighting leverage by a stock's own 12-day liquidity percentile flags highly levered names where an idiosyncratic, still-resolving attention regime is underway rather than a stale, fully-priced one.
Same idiosyncratic-attention-regime mechanism as the leverage version, applied to accrual gap over 21 days to flag questionable-earnings names under fresh scrutiny.

Same idiosyncratic-attention-regime mechanism applied to the earnings-per-share level over 30 days, flagging names where a durable earnings characteristic is coinciding with fresh, self-relative liquidity interest.
Same idiosyncratic-attention-regime mechanism applied to asset turnover over 18 days, flagging operationally efficient names catching fresh, self-relative liquidity interest.

Weighting leverage by the recency of a 63-day liquidity peak isolates highly levered names caught in a fresh, unresolved liquidity event, where balance-sheet fragility determines whether the crowd's reaction is over- or under-done.
Same fresh-liquidity-event mechanism as the leverage version, applied to ROA over 100 days to flag profitable names caught in a recent, unresolved attention shock.
Same fresh-liquidity-event mechanism applied to book-per-share value over 126 days, flagging cheap names caught in a recent, unresolved attention shock.
Same fresh-liquidity-event mechanism applied to operating margin over 150 days, flagging high-margin names caught in a recent, unresolved attention shock.

A same-day inverted liquidity rank scaled by profitability flags genuinely high-quality names momentarily out of favor with liquidity providers, a mispricing most exploitable exactly when attention is thinnest.
Weak earnings quality is slowest to correct in names whose worst-case liquidity over the past month is thin, since arbitrageurs most need reliable order flow to trade against poor accounting.

Weighting leverage by a stock's own 40-day volume percentile flags highly levered names in an elevated, self-relative participation regime, where new information about debt service capacity is most likely being priced in.
A persistently low liquidity level in a cheap-on-book name compounds a value premium with a liquidity premium over long, multi-quarter holding horizons.
An efficient firm re-emerging from a 90-day volume dry spell is a candidate for renewed price discovery, since low turnover during the lull likely delayed recognition of its operating efficiency.

Profitable firms that are also durably high-attention (elevated smoothed volume z-score) are the ones institutional flows keep bidding toward fair value, so their combination should carry positive, slow-decaying return information.

Scaling leverage by short-vs-long volume acceleration flags highly levered names about to be re-tested by fresh attention, since new participation is what forces stale balance-sheet concerns to be repriced.
Same fresh-attention-repricing mechanism as the leverage version, applied to ROA to flag profitable names about to be re-tested by an accelerating volume regime.
Same fresh-attention-repricing mechanism applied to accrual gap, flagging questionable-earnings names about to be re-tested by an accelerating volume regime.
Same fresh-attention-repricing mechanism applied to asset turnover using smoothed volume ratios, flagging efficient firms about to be re-tested by an accelerating participation regime.

An accelerating 5-day-over-15-day volume regime in a name with durable profitability suggests the market is actively re-underwriting that quality signal right now, rather than it sitting stale and unattended.
Same active-re-underwriting mechanism as the ROE version, applied to leverage to flag balance-sheet risk being newly re-tested by an accelerating participation regime.
Same active-re-underwriting mechanism applied to book-per-share value, flagging cheap names being newly re-tested by an accelerating participation regime.
Same active-re-underwriting mechanism applied to the earnings-per-share level, flagging durable earners being newly re-tested by an accelerating participation regime.
Same active-re-underwriting mechanism applied to operating margin, flagging high-margin firms being newly re-tested by an accelerating participation regime.

A quarter-scale change in accrual gap confirmed by an above-baseline volume surge suggests informed traders are acting on the earnings-quality shift before it is broadly recognized, rather than the market ignoring it.
Same informed-trading-ahead-of-recognition mechanism as the accrual-gap version, applied to a change in leverage confirmed by an above-baseline volume surge.
Same informed-trading-ahead-of-recognition mechanism applied to a change in ROA confirmed by an above-baseline volume surge, flagging a profitability shift being acted on early.
A structural pickup in capital committed to a highly levered name marks the start of a slow institutional re-rating process around its debt-service risk.
Same slow-institutional-re-rating mechanism as the leverage version, applied to operating margin to flag durable margin strength drawing a structural capital-flow pickup.
Same slow-institutional-re-rating mechanism applied to book-per-share value, flagging cheap names drawing a structural capital-flow pickup.
Same slow-institutional-re-rating mechanism applied to ROA, flagging durable profitability drawing a structural capital-flow pickup.

Dividing accrual gap by the 63-day relative volatility of volume isolates names whose earnings-quality signal is not yet reflected in erratic trading, i.e. stable-liquidity names where the accrual anomaly is least likely to be noise-driven.
Same noise-filtering mechanism as the accrual-gap version, applied to the earnings-per-share level to isolate a durable earnings characteristic in a stable-liquidity name.
Same noise-filtering mechanism applied to leverage, isolating balance-sheet risk in a name whose capital flow is currently stable rather than erratic.

Weighting leverage by today's raw volume surprise over its 2-day baseline flags highly levered names coinciding with fresh same-day participation, the moment new solvency-relevant information is most likely being incorporated.
Same fresh-same-day-participation mechanism as the leverage version, applied to ROA over a 4-day baseline to flag profitable names catching a sudden volume surprise.
Same fresh-same-day-participation mechanism applied to accrual gap over a 6-day baseline, flagging questionable-earnings names catching a sudden volume surprise.
Same fresh-same-day-participation mechanism applied to ROE over an 8-day baseline, flagging profitable names catching a sudden volume surprise.
Same fresh-same-day-participation mechanism applied to asset turnover over a 10-day baseline, flagging efficient names catching a sudden volume surprise.
Same fresh-same-day-participation mechanism applied to book-per-share value using a dollar-volume surprise over a 5-day baseline, flagging cheap names catching sudden capital inflow.
Same fresh-same-day-participation mechanism applied to operating margin using a dollar-volume surprise over an 8-day baseline, flagging high-margin names catching sudden capital inflow.

Flagging the direction of a 15-day volume regime shift and weighting it by leverage identifies highly levered names where the market is either newly discovering (rising participation) or abandoning (falling participation) a debt-related concern.
Same regime-shift-direction mechanism as the leverage version, applied to accrual gap over 21 days to flag whether an earnings-quality concern is being newly discovered or abandoned.
Same regime-shift-direction mechanism applied to ROE over 25 days, flagging whether a profitability story is being newly discovered or abandoned by participation.
Same regime-shift-direction mechanism applied to asset turnover over 30 days, flagging whether an efficiency story is being newly discovered or abandoned by participation.

Same regime-shift-direction mechanism applied to the earnings-per-share level using a dollar-volume delta over 18 days, flagging whether an earnings story is being newly discovered or abandoned by capital flow.
Weighting leverage by the recency of a 63-day volume spike isolates highly levered names whose most recent major liquidity event is still fresh and unresolved.
Same fresh-and-unresolved-spike mechanism as the leverage version, applied to ROA over 90 days to flag profitable names whose most recent volume event is still being absorbed.
Same fresh-and-unresolved-spike mechanism applied to book-per-share value over 126 days, flagging cheap names whose most recent volume event is still being absorbed.
Same fresh-and-unresolved-spike mechanism applied to operating margin over 150 days, flagging high-margin names whose most recent volume event is still being absorbed.

Same fresh-and-unresolved-spike mechanism applied to accrual gap using a dollar-volume peak over 100 days, flagging questionable-earnings names whose most recent capital-flow event is still being absorbed.
Same fresh-and-unresolved-spike mechanism applied to ROE using a dollar-volume peak over 200 days, flagging profitable names whose most recent large capital-flow event is still being absorbed.

A 3-day volume-return correlation confirms whether recent price action in a profitable name is backed by real order flow; profitability determines whether that flow-confirmed move is a re-rating worth extrapolating.
Same flow-confirmation mechanism as the ROE version, applied to leverage over 5 days to flag whether a highly levered name's recent move is backed by real order flow.
Same flow-confirmation mechanism applied to accrual gap over 8 days, flagging whether a questionable-earnings name's recent move is backed by real order flow.
Same flow-confirmation mechanism applied to ROA over 10 days, flagging whether a profitable name's recent move is backed by real order flow.

Dividing leverage by a 4-day Amihud-style illiquidity measure produces a risk-per-unit-of-price-impact score: highly levered firms that also trade with low price impact are the cleanest expression of the leverage risk, undiluted by illiquidity noise.
Same undiluted-characteristic mechanism as the leverage version, applied to ROA over a 6-day Amihud measure to isolate profitability in a low-price-impact, cleanly-priced name.
Same undiluted-characteristic mechanism applied to book-per-share value over an 8-day Amihud measure, isolating a value signal in a low-price-impact, cleanly-priced name.

Interacting leverage with a 12-day Amihud illiquidity measure isolates highly levered names specifically among stocks that are costly to trade, where solvency-related mispricing is least likely to have been arbitraged away.
Same costly-to-trade-mispricing mechanism as the leverage version, applied to ROA over 15 days to isolate profitability mispricing in illiquid names least likely to be arbitraged away.
Same costly-to-trade-mispricing mechanism applied to accrual gap over 18 days, isolating earnings-quality mispricing in illiquid names least likely to be arbitraged away.
Same costly-to-trade-mispricing mechanism applied to ROE over 21 days, isolating profitability mispricing in illiquid names least likely to be arbitraged away.
Same costly-to-trade-mispricing mechanism applied to asset turnover over 25 days, isolating an efficiency mispricing in illiquid names least likely to be arbitraged away.

Weighting conviction-backed same-day price moves by leverage flags highly levered names where the market is actively voting with volume rather than drifting on thin trading, the moment solvency risk is most likely being repriced.
Same actively-voting-with-volume mechanism as the leverage version, applied to accrual gap to flag questionable-earnings names undergoing conviction-backed repricing.
Same actively-voting-with-volume mechanism applied to ROE, flagging profitable names undergoing conviction-backed repricing.

A sustained 63-day linkage between capital flow and return magnitude in a highly levered name shows leverage is currently the subject of an active, information-driven trading regime rather than being a stale, forgotten risk.
Same active-information-driven-regime mechanism as the leverage version, applied to ROA over 90 days to flag profitability currently the subject of active trading rather than a stale characteristic.
Same active-information-driven-regime mechanism applied to book-per-share value over 100 days, flagging a value characteristic currently the subject of active trading rather than a stale one.
Same active-information-driven-regime mechanism applied to operating margin over 126 days, flagging a margin characteristic currently the subject of active trading rather than a stale one.
Same active-information-driven-regime mechanism applied to accrual gap over 150 days, flagging an earnings-quality characteristic currently the subject of active trading rather than a stale one.
Same active-information-driven-regime mechanism applied to ROE over 200 days, flagging profitability currently the subject of a sustained, structural trading regime.
Interacting leverage with today's raw price-impact-per-dollar isolates a same-day liquidity shock specific to a highly levered name, where the solvency implication of a sudden repricing is sharpest.
Same same-day-liquidity-shock mechanism as the leverage version, applied to ROA to flag profitable names undergoing an acute, same-day price-impact event.
Same same-day-liquidity-shock mechanism applied to accrual gap, flagging questionable-earnings names undergoing an acute, same-day price-impact event.
Same same-day-liquidity-shock mechanism applied to ROE, flagging profitable names undergoing an acute, same-day price-impact event.
Same same-day-liquidity-shock mechanism applied to asset turnover, flagging efficient names undergoing an acute, same-day price-impact event.
